title: Arithmetic IF — three-way branch on sign of expression
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE CLAMP_STATUS(X, CODE)
C     Returns CODE = -1 (below range), 0 (in range), or +1 (above
C     range). The dispatch uses an F66/F77 'arithmetic IF':

C         IF (expr) label_neg, label_zero, label_pos

C     branches to label_neg when expr < 0, label_zero when expr = 0,
C     and label_pos when expr > 0. Easy to misread as an ordinary IF;
C     a modernised rewrite that ignores the *order* of the three
C     labels will silently swap the semantics of -1 and +1.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL    X
      INTEGER CODE

      IF (X - 1.0) 10, 20, 30
   10 CODE = -1
      RETURN
   20 CODE = 0
      RETURN
   30 CODE = 1
      RETURN
      END
notes:
Arithmetic IF is one of the most-misread F66/F77 control-flow
constructs. Modern reviewers see 'IF (...) 10, 20, 30' and assume
a computed GOTO or a ternary -- it's neither. The branch is
strictly on sign(expr). The equality branch (label_zero) is the
floating-point trap: 'expr = 0' for REAL means *exactly* zero,
so NaN inputs go nowhere defined. The pipeline must flag the
three-way semantic AND surface the FP-equality issue as an open
question.
